read_seed_points_log.get_state_at_iteration()¶

Extract a “state” from a seed_point_log where all the seed coordinates are given on one line for for one iteration

Parameters:
  • state_array (numpy array) – Iterations extracted from a seed_point_log.csv file
  • iteration (int) – Iteration at which we want to get the state
Returns:

state_at_iteration – Coordinates of seed points at the specified iteration
Return type:

numpy array
read_seed_points_log.read_seed_points()¶

Read the coordinates in a csv file with the following format: |[x0_0 y0_0]| |[x1_0 y1_0]| … |[x0_1 y0_1]| |[x1_1 y1_1]| … And convert them into a numpy array.

Parameters:filename (string) – Name of the csv log file
Returns:
  • filename (string)
  • data_read_array (numpy array) – Parsed data from the csv log file. Every row contains the position of every seed points for an iteration. Each row represents an iteration.
read_seed_points_log.reconstruct_state_at_iteration()¶

Reads from a seed_point_log.csv file and extracts the position of every seed points at a given iteration. Generate a periodic tesselation around the observation box.

Note : this is a convenience function for one call. If multiple calls, use read_seed_points() once, and then call get_state_at_iteration and periodic boundaries as needed.

Parameters:
  • filename (string) – Name of the seed poing log csv file.
  • iteration (int) – Desired iteration to reconstruct
  • boxsize (float) –
Returns:

  • state (numpy array) – Array of seed points coordinates at the specified iteration
  • extended_points (numpy array) – state + periodic boundaric conditions around the observation box
